description: What an advanced search (many keywords across many places) would find and how long it would take — without starting it or spending anything. expected_leads is the most likely number of unique leads (each business is charged once however many keywords or places find it); low–high is the range it lands in most of the time.

country.description: 'US' (the default), or a US territory's code ('PR', 'GU', 'VI', 'AS', 'MP') with a place from find_places.

everywhere.description: Every place in the US (or in the territory sent as country).

keywords.description: What to search for: up to 20 keywords or Google categories, each up to 100 characters. Each a string, or { keyword, exact } where exact keeps only businesses whose main Google category is that one.

lead_cap.description: Stop after this many unique, charged leads: a whole number from 100 to 1,000,000. Omit to search every place.

places.description: Single places by name ('Austin'), 'name, region' when a name is in several ('Springfield, Illinois'), or code (find_places). Up to 25,000 regions and places together; keywords × places may come to at most 50,000 searches.

regions.description: Whole US states, by name or code (find_places).

name: estimate_advanced_search

campaign_searches_per_day.description: Places a day advanced searches may use on this plan.

charged_leads.description: Leads expected to be charged: expected_leads, capped by lead_cap.

keywords.description: Each { keyword, exact }, as they would run.

paced_by_daily_budget.description: True when the account's daily city budget, not the searching, sets the time.

time.description: How long it would take, waits for the daily city budget included.

title: Estimate an advanced search
